title: Film, Commercial & Documentary Production Permits in Türkiye
seoTitle: Film Permit Turkey: Crew Rules, ATA Carnet & Drone Guide
metaDescription: How foreign crews secure a film permit in Türkiye: Ministry rules, local fixers, ATA Carnet gear customs, SHGM drone permits, and heritage site fees.
quickAnswer: Foreign film, commercial, and documentary crews shooting in Türkiye must obtain a national filming permit from the Ministry of Culture and Tourism's Directorate General of Cinema and appoint a mandatory Turkish-citizen fixer (mihmandar). Camera gear enters duty-free via ATA Carnet, while drones require separate SHGM clearance and heritage sites charge dedicated location fees.

body.text: How do foreign crews obtain Ministry of Culture filming permits and local fixers?

Foreign producers, directors, and production companies apply online through the Ministry of Culture and Tourism's Directorate General of Cinema portal (filmingpermit.ktb.gov.tr), submitting a synopsis and script in Turkish, crew lists, equipment manifests, and shooting schedules. Turkish regulations make it mandatory to engage at least one Turkish-citizen host or fixer (mihmandar) throughout the shoot.

Per the official [Directorate General of Cinema Filming Permit guidelines](https://sinema.ktb.gov.tr/TR-143934/yabanci-yapimlar-icin-cekim-izni-filming-permit.html) and [Filming in Türkiye](https://www.filminginturkiye.com.tr/), the fixer coordinates municipal street clearances, governorship notifications, and the mandatory post-shoot evaluation form. Productions qualifying for Türkiye's cash rebate of up to 30% on local spend must also partner with a registered Turkish production service company.

[Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/) is an independent, client-paid, flat-fee advisory run by its two founders in Türkiye ("Paid by our clients. Independent of provider commissions."). We organize location-scouting itineraries, crew accommodation, private vans, and vetted introductions to licensed fixers; formal filming permits, visa/work-permit exemptions, SHGM drone applications, and ATA Carnet customs clearances belong strictly to licensed fixers, Turkish attorneys, customs brokers, and official authorities.
What customs rules (ATA Carnet) apply to camera and drone gear?

Professional camera, lighting, and sound packages enter Türkiye duty- and VAT-free temporarily under an ATA Carnet issued by your home chamber of commerce and recognized by Turkish Customs and TOBB. Drones face stricter rules: aircraft of 500 grams or more require advance technical conformity and flight authorization from the Civil Aviation Directorate (SHGM).

According to the [Union of Chambers and Commodity Exchanges of Türkiye (TOBB) ATA Carnet Division](https://tobb.org.tr/TIRIslemleriMudurlugu/ATA/Sayfalar/Eng/ATANedir.php) and the [Turkish Film Commission ATA Carnet guide](https://turkishfilmcommission.org/ata-carnet-for-film-productions-in-turkiye/), serial numbers on every lens, body, and battery case must match the Carnet manifest exactly at arrival and departure customs. For aerial units, the [SHGM UAS Registry System](https://iha.shgm.gov.tr/public/index?language=2) mandates prior import approval and airspace clearance—so many visiting commercial crews hire a locally registered Turkish drone operator with an active SHGM license instead of importing foreign airframes.
Which heritage sites (Hagia Sophia, Ephesus, Cappadocia) require extra location fees?

A national Directorate General of Cinema permit does not automatically grant access to museums, archaeological ruins, active mosques, or protected natural parks. Iconic locations such as Hagia Sophia, Ephesus, Topkapı Palace, and Cappadocia's valleys require separate site-level approvals, fixed daily commercial location fees, and strict restrictions on tripods, lighting rigs, and crew headcounts.

Archaeological zones like the [Ephesus Archaeological Site](https://muze.gov.tr/Language/Index/EN?url=%2Fmuze-detay%3Fsectionid%3Defs01%26distid%3Defs) fall under Ministry of Culture and Tourism museum directives, while active religious landmarks such as Hagia Sophia involve additional religious-authority coordination and prayer-time blackouts. Cappadocia shoots require clearance from the Cappadocia Area Presidency and local governorships, with separate commercial daily tariffs and strict no-fly zones during morning hot-air balloon launches.
How far ahead must permits be filed?

File general Ministry of Culture filming permits at least 10 to 15 business days before arrival, even though straightforward documentary applications sometimes clear in five to seven working days. Productions involving heritage sites, street closures, or SHGM foreign drone permits should submit complete dossiers four to six weeks ahead of principal photography.

body.text: Use this pre-production readiness checklist before locking flights:

items: Appoint a Turkish fixer early: Confirm your named mihmandar before opening the filmingpermit.ktb.gov.tr file.
Translate project documents: Prepare Turkish translations of your synopsis, script, and location breakdown.
Decide on local vs. imported drones: Hiring a licensed local SHGM operator avoids multi-week customs holds.
Audit ATA Carnet serials: Reconcile every camera body, lens, and recorder serial number before airport check-in.
Build weather and prayer buffers: Account for Friday prayers in Istanbul and balloon-flight airspace windows in Cappadocia.

faq.q: Can a foreign documentary or commercial crew film in Türkiye without a local fixer?
faq.a: No. Directorate General of Cinema regulations require every foreign production filming in Türkiye to appoint at least one Turkish-citizen host/fixer (mihmandar) and submit an end-of-shoot evaluation report.

faq.q: How does Türkiye's 30% foreign film production cash rebate work?
faq.a: The Ministry of Culture and Tourism administers a cash rebate of up to 30% on qualifying local production spend for eligible foreign feature films, TV series, and documentaries, processed through licensed Turkish service producers.

faq.q: Can foreign crews bring a drone into Türkiye as checked luggage without prior approval?
faq.a: No. Drones weighing 500 grams or more require prior SHGM technical conformity approval and flight authorization; undeclared drones are routinely held by airport customs until departure.

faq.q: Does a general Ministry filming permit cover Ephesus or Hagia Sophia?
faq.a: No. The national filming permit is only the first step; archaeological sites, museums, mosques, and Cappadocia valleys require separate site-specific approvals and daily location fees.

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye file Ministry filming permits or ATA Carnets?
faq.a: No. We coordinate scouting logistics, crew transport, hotels, and independent introductions to licensed Turkish fixers and customs brokers, who submit official permits, SHGM filings, and ATA Carnets.

faq.q: Do foreign crew members need a special film visa or can they enter on a tourist visa?
faq.a: Official guidance states that foreign crews with filming permits should check consular visa and work-permit-exemption rules with the Turkish Embassy or a licensed Turkish immigration attorney before travel.
